title: Time 1: Который час? (час / часа / часов)
description: To say what o'clock it is, count the hours: один час, два часа, пять часов. The word for 'hour' changes with the number: 1 takes час, 2-4 take часа, 5 and up take часов. This is the core numeral-agreement rule, met first on the clock.
descriptionRussian: Чтобы сказать, который час, считают часы: один час, два часа, пять часов. Слово «час» меняется в зависимости от числа: 1 — час, 2–4 — часа, 5 и больше — часов. Это основное правило согласования числительных, которое мы сначала встречаем на часах.
intro: Telling the time in Russian is the counting rule from A1 wearing a hat. One hour, two through four hours, five and above: the word for 'hour' takes three forms and switches at exactly the same borders as every other counted noun. If that book stuck, this lesson is mostly vocabulary.
rules: Ask the time with Который час? ('which hour?'). Answer by counting the hours and attaching the right form of час.
The number 1 (один) takes час: Сейчас час. The один is optional; bare час is common in speech.
The numbers 2, 3, 4 take часа: два часа, три часа, четыре часа.
The numbers 5 through 12 take часов: пять часов, восемь часов, двенадцать часов.

To mark the part of the day, add a genitive word after the hours: два часа дня (2 p.m.), семь часов утра (7 a.m.), девять часов вечера (9 p.m.), три часа ночи (3 a.m.). It does not change the час/часа/часов choice.
examples: Сейчас час. (It is one o'clock.) 1 → час.
Сейчас два часа. (It is two o'clock.) 2 → часа.
Сейчас четыре часа. (It is four o'clock.) 4 → часа.
Сейчас пять часов. (It is five o'clock.) 5 → часов.
Сейчас десять часов. (It is ten o'clock.) 10 → часов.
Сейчас семь часов утра. (It is seven in the morning.) 7 → часов, plus genitive утра for the part of day.

tables.title: The hour count: 1 → час, 2-4 → часа, 5+ → часов

items.explanation: After 2, 3, and 4 the noun takes the form часа: два часа, три часа, четыре часа. So 'two o'clock' is два часа.

items.hint: From 5 upward the noun switches to a different form.
items.explanation: Numbers 5 through 12 take часов: пять часов, восемь часов, двенадцать часов. So 'five o'clock' is пять часов.

items.hint: For one o'clock the noun stays in its dictionary form. The number один is usually dropped.
items.explanation: One o'clock is simply час (or один час). The number 1 takes the singular dictionary form час, and in speech the один is normally left out.
3 belongs to the 2-4 group, which takes часа: два часа, три часа, четыре часа. So 'three o'clock' is три часа.

items.hint: 10 is firmly in the '5 and up' group.
items.explanation: Every number from 5 to 12 takes часов, and 10 is no exception: десять часов.

items.promptEnglish: It is seven in the morning.
items.hint: The number is 7. The word утра at the end does not change the hour form.
items.explanation: 7 takes часов: семь часов. Adding утра (genitive, 'in the morning') marks the part of the day but never changes the час/часа/часов choice, which depends only on the number.

fillInBlank.grammarFocus: 4 belongs to the 2-4 group, so the noun takes часа: четыре часа. The forms час (after 1) and часов (after 5+) would be wrong here.

categorySorting.instruction: Sort each number by the form of 'hour' it takes.

errorCorrection.explanation: The numbers 2, 3, and 4 take the special 'few' form часа: два часа, три часа, четыре часа. Часов is the form for 5 and up (пять часов), so it is wrong after 3. The correct phrase is три часа.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: It is eight in the evening.
errorCorrection.explanation: Every number from 5 through 12 takes часов: пять часов, восемь часов, двенадцать часов. Часа is only for the 2-4 group (три часа), so it is wrong after 8. The genitive part-of-day word вечера ('in the evening') never changes the час/часа/часов choice, which depends only on the number. The correct phrase is восемь часов вечера.

The number 1 (один) takes the bare singular dictionary form час: один час, or simply час in speech. Часов is the 5-and-up form (пять часов), so it is wrong here. So 'one o'clock' is один час, not один часов. The correct answer is час.

minimalPairs.explanation: 2 belongs to the 2-4 group, which takes часа. Часов is the 5-and-up form, so 'два часов' is wrong. Correct: два часа.
6 is in the '5 and up' group, so it takes часов: шесть часов. Часа is only for 2, 3, 4, so 'шесть часа' is wrong.

reviewVocab.definition: What time is it? The standard way to ask the clock time (literally 'which hour?').
the three forms of 'hour' chosen by the number: 1 → час, 2-4 → часа, 5 and up → часов. This is the core numeral-agreement pattern.
reviewVocab.example: один час, два часа, пять часов.

reviewVocab.definition: genitive part-of-day words added after the hour to say morning / afternoon / evening / night. They do not change the час/часа/часов choice.
reviewVocab.example: семь часов утра, два часа дня, девять часов вечера.
